utterances.text: So the number of casualties from the 306th Mountain Brigade in total numbered about 136 from November 1992 through December 1995.

utterances.speaker: ESED SIPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, yes, as far as I can recall. Because there was an analysis made. So as far as I can recall, that's the number and there were also about 400 wounded mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sipic, when you talked with this man who introduced himself as the Emir of the Mujahedin, at the time did you know who was behind these Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ESED SIPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I absolutely did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the conversation, did you notice whether he respected you as a commander of a brigade or whether his conduct towards you was --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why? Why the objection? Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, this doesn't arise directly out of the questions that the Trial Chamber put to the witness on this issue. These questions could have been asked in direct examination or even in -- in redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, I did tackle the issue of his encounter with the Emir and it seems useful to me to obtain some detail. Can you please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sipic, in your conversation with them, did you notice whether he felt that you were not at his level or that you were superior to him during your conversation?

utterances.speaker: ESED SIPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I felt so uncomfortable. I had the feeling that he could kill me. He simply ignored me. This was very short. Simply his words to me led me to have nothing more to ask him and I simply wanted to leave the camp as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have just told the President of the Trial Chamber that you don't know whether he was in communication with Mr. Halilovic or not. But based on that conversation, were you able to conclude that he was behaving as if somebody powerful was backing him?

utterances.speaker: ESED SIPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have just one brief question arising from the question asked by the Trial Chamber's President, referring to the HOS. You have already replied that the HOS became a part of the HVO. Do you know what its position was in 1993? Was the HOS part of the HVO already in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ESED SIPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned how they were dressed, and you said that they wore black and wore the insignia, a letter "U." Could you please tell us what this letter "U" indicated, and did it mean the same thing to all the people in that region?

utterances.speaker: ESED SIPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me, as a person, associated that with World War II, because in films as a child I would see the Ustasha wearing the same uniforms, black uniforms with the letter "U" and also with knives that they had at their belts. So I as a commander and the majority of my officers linked that with supporting and following the tradition of the Ustashas.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All the people, whether they were young or old, did they all know who the Ustashas were?

utterances.speaker: ESED SIPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my area, where I was, they all did know that and they had reason to do so because many of them were the victims of these Ustashas. They looked so terrible. Please believe me that everybody avoided encountering them on the streets because their impression was just so frightening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The other Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, your testimony is now finished. I would like to thank you for coming to testify, for having answered the questions put to you by both parties and by the Trial Chamber. We wish you a happy journey back home. And I'm going to ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I'm turning to the Defence to see if they have any exhibits to tender into evidence. Maybe you prefer to do it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would rather do that tomorrow, but I would like to ask to go into private session briefly because I would like to address you on another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, very briefly. We are -- let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is ten past 7.00. I would like to invite all of you present here to come back for the session is that starts tomorrow at quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 27th day of January, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25
